title: Winter elms at middle distance carry twice the twigs
items: With the Season set to winter, the bare elms a short walk away (about 10 to 45 m) now carry twice as many fine twigs, so their crowns grey in against the sky the way the elms do in Taylor's winter photograph of the Pullman estate.
A tree costs the same to draw as before: each twig at that distance is a thin taper rather than a full stroke, which is all a twig under a pixel wide needs.
Near trees, far trees, and trees in summer, spring and fall are unchanged.
